ordered_diagnoses: Cholangiocarcinoma of the extrahepatic bile duct

s1.syndrome_frame: Right upper abdominal pain with mass and abnormal liver function
salient_findings: Heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa
key_facts: 64-year-old woman
2-month history of right upper abdominal pain
No nausea, vomiting, chills, or fever
Afebrile and oriented on examination
Right upper abdominal tenderness without rebound or palpable masses
No hepatosplenomegaly
Negative Murphy’s sign and shifting dullness
Elevated WBC count
Elevated CA19-9 level
Presence of gallstones and gallbladder wall thickening
Enhanced pancreatic echogenicity on ultrasonography
Lesion in the right hepatic lobe adjacent to the gallbladder fossa on CT
Multiple enlarged hepatic hilar lymph nodes on CT

shortlist: Cholangiocarcinoma of the extrahepatic bile duct

shortlist.label: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CA19-9 level and lesion in the right hepatic lobe adjacent to the gallbladder fossa on CT

shortlist.label: Gallbladder cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of gallstones and gallbladder wall thickening, and lesion in the right hepatic lobe adjacent to the gallbladder fossa on CT

shortlist.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated AFP level and lesion in the right hepatic lobe on ultrasonography and CT

shortlist.label: Cholangiocarcinoma of the extrahepatic bile duct
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CA19-9 level and multiple enlarged hepatic hilar lymph nodes on CT

shortlist.label: Hepatic metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple lesions in the liver and elevated tumor markers

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of right upper abdominal pain, elevated CA19-9 level, and imaging findings of a lesion in the right hepatic lobe adjacent to the gallbladder fossa, along with mild intrahepatic bile duct dilatation, are consistent with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Gallbladder cancer
rejected.why: While gallstones and gallbladder wall thickening are present, the primary lesion is in the liver, not the gallbladder.

rejected.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
rejected.why: The patient's AFP level is within normal limits, which is unusual for hepatocellular carcinoma.

rejected.label: Cholangiocarcinoma of the extrahepatic bile duct
rejected.why: No extrahepatic primary tumor was identified, and the lesion is located in the right hepatic lobe.

rejected.label: Hepatic metastasis
rejected.why: There is no mention of a primary tumor outside the liver, and the presentation is more consistent with a primary liver malignancy.
